title: Electric Service Agreement Repeat-Lateness Window and Automatic Payments: Decision Table
content:
For an Electric Service Agreement, the repeat-lateness window — the period over which the late payment charges already posted on the agreement are counted when a new late payment charge is posted — is set by the automatic (autopay) payments the agreement received in the 12 calendar months before this charge, because a customer who has been paying automatically is judged on recent conduct.

## Decision table

| Autopay payments received on the agreement in the 12 calendar months before this charge | Repeat-lateness window |
|---|---|
| 6 or more | the 1 calendar month before this charge |
| 3 to 5 | the 3 calendar months before this charge |
| fewer than 3 (0, 1 or 2) | the 12 calendar months before this charge |

**Counting rule.** Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date. This applies both to the autopay payments counted over the 12 calendar months and to the late payment charges counted over the window the table selects. Only payments received through the autopay channel are counted as autopay payments.

## Boundary rows

- 5 autopay payments: 3-month window. 6 autopay payments: 1-month window.
- 2 autopay payments: 12-month window. 3 autopay payments: 3-month window.

## Illustration (hypothetical dates)

A late payment charge is to be posted on a hypothetical 20 March. The agreement received 7 autopay payments in the 12 calendar months before, so the window is the 1 calendar month before the posting: a late payment charge dated 25 February is inside it (less than one whole month before 20 March), while one dated 20 February is not (exactly one whole month before). Had the agreement received only 4 autopay payments, the window would be the 3 calendar months before 20 March, and both charges would fall inside it.
